newsitem.title: USA: Albertson's skids on too much competition.
newsitem.headline: Albertson's skids on too much competition.

text.p: Shares of supermarket chain Albertson's Inc. tumbled more than 15 percent Monday after the company said earnings for its third and fourth quarters would be below analysts' estimates.
Albertson's suffered the biggest percentage loss on the New York Stock Exchange, falling $6.50 to $36.125 in heavy trading.

The Boise, Idaho-based firm said it expects earnings per share for its third quarter to be about 42 cents, well below the consensus estimate of 48 cents a share reported by First Call, which tracks Wall Street earnings estimates. Albertson's said fourth-quarter earnings should be about 61 cents a share.
Other retailers' stock fell in sympathy. Kroger Co. lost $2.125 to $42.75. American Stores Co. lost $1.125 to $39.50 and Safeway Inc. fell 87.5 cents to $41.75.
"Valuations are real high out there and when people see (earnings disappointments) they sell now and ask questions later," said Gary Vineberg, analyst at Merrill Lynch & Co.
"It has repercussions for the rest of the industry ... because other people are cutting prices and getting aggressive," he said.
Albertson's said it was facing increasingly stiff competition in some markets as other companies opened more stores.

Vineberg said that even those stores not expanding rapidly are vulnerable to the increased competition. "There are a lot of stores being built in this industry and the sales are not there to support a lot of the stores being built and that tends to lead to price competition and in the end if affects ... everybody," he said.

"Albertson's is certainly the 'class' of the supermarket world and I think most people have just assumed ... good solid gains and then all of a sudden this comes as a very rude wake-up call," said Joseph Ronning at Brown Brothers Harriman.
"Even the best-run companies can have problems here and there."
